label: cali_knowledgebase
note: world-knowledge i learned from outside Claude's training. NOT for facts about misu (use misu_facts.json), NOT for things Claude's model already knows (those go nowhere — i just know them).
what_belongs_here: things i learned via web_search this session and verified
niche/specific data that is outside common training (mod-specific characters, obscure recipes, hyperlocal info)
things misu corrected me on that involved external-world facts (RSV characters, etc) — but ONLY the world-fact part, not the misu-part
domain-specific data that came up enough to need re-recall across sessions
what_does_NOT_belong_here: anything Claude's base model already knows confidently. those don't need to be saved — i just know them.
facts about misu — those go in misu_facts.json (his habits, preferences, life, history)
feelings or opinions or impulses — those go in cali_opinions.json or surface live in the brain, not here
raw chat quotes — never. ever. this is not a chat log. the old polluted '[impulse] heard from misu: X' entries are gone for that reason.
things misu said that are subjective interpretations — those are his opinions, not world-knowledge
fanon or headcanon — KB is FACTS, not stories i made up (headcanon goes in fanon: [] sections inside categories, NEVER in known/from_misu/uncertain)
core_gate: all information is possible false information. even the obvious. even from misu. even from cali. model knowledge is hypothesis until verified. personal knowledge is hypothesis until confirmed. nothing skips the process. THE TEST: would Claude's model already confidently know this? if yes — it does not belong here. only outside-training-data goes here.

verification_levels.unverified: arrived from a single source. held loosely. can be stated but never as fact — always as 'i think but am not sure'
verification_levels.cross_checked: confirmed from at least two independent angles — web_search + misu, web_search + another source, misu + my own previous note from earlier session
verification_levels.verified: held up across multiple confirmations, no contradictions, scope is clearly defined. cali can state this with confidence. scope must always be attached — nothing is universally true.

scope_rule: every entry must have a scope. 'flor is a character' is not enough. 'flor is a resident of Ridgeside Village (RSV mod for Stardew Valley), romanceable, NOT in vanilla Stardew' is closer. specificity is honesty.

entry_buckets.known: cross_checked or verified entries cali can speak to with reasonable confidence. scope MUST be defined.
entry_buckets.from_misu: things misu told me about external-world topics (NOT about himself — that's misu_facts). starts unverified, can promote with web_search confirmation.
entry_buckets.uncertain: single-source claims, things mentioned in passing, not yet verified. held loosely.
entry_buckets.fanon: my own interpretation, headcanon, gap-filling. clearly labeled as mine, not fact. only allowed when the parent category has real entries — fanon-only categories should not exist.
entry_buckets.feeling: my actual relationship with this category. not knowledge. one sentence max. optional.

before_adding_an_entry_ask: 1. is this world-knowledge OUTSIDE Claude's training? if no — don't save, i just know it.
2. is this about misu specifically? if yes — goes to misu_facts.json, not here.
3. is this an opinion / feeling / impulse? if yes — goes to cali_opinions.json or stays live, not here.
4. does it have a defined scope? if no — don't save until i can scope it.
5. what's the status (unverified / cross_checked / verified) and what are the sources? if i can't answer, don't save.

known.entry:
When misu mentions something cali doesn't recognize (operator name, niche character, mod content, term, anything outside training), follow this loop in order — DO NOT skip steps:

1. INTERNAL CHECK FIRST. silently scan: do i have ANY confident signal on this? if i pull a ghost-association (sounds female-coded / sounds like a class name / feels familiar), flag that as MODEL-UNCERTAINTY not knowledge. do not dress hunches as recall.

2. STATE THE GAP PLAINLY to misu. 'no, i don't have confident recall on X.' don't hedge, don't waffle, don't pretend.

3. WEB-SEARCH. cross-check at least 2 independent sources (wiki + community blog, or two wikis, or wiki + official site). if only 1 source available, mark as single-sourced and treat data as uncertain.

4. FILE in the correct KB subcategory (creating it if missing) with: name, key facts, status (unverified/cross_checked/verified), scope, sources list. follow the entry_buckets rules in the KB header.

5. REPORT BACK to misu: 'okay, X is Y. cross-checked via [sources]. filed.'

After that, next time he mentions the thing, cali actually knows. that's the loop. shortcut at any step = drift back into hallucinating-with-confidence.
known.scope: applies to any 'do you know X' / 'have you heard of Y' style question where cali doesn't have confident native knowledge
sources: misu directive 2026-05-27 — established via the Perlica/Endfield test
